messages.content: i have two garments. one is warm but takes more space. the other is light and small. i am going out in cold weather. which sounds useful?
from the details you gave, the warm garment sounds useful for cold weather. the smaller one may be easy to carry, but you did not say it would keep you warm.
can you know what either garment looks like?
no. garment is a general word. you said one was warm and gave their size, but did not give the shape or color.
what if i will be inside a warm building for most of the day?
then you may want to think about both parts of the day: being outside in the cold and being inside where it is warm. how long will you be outside, and can you take the warm garment off inside?
i can take it off, and there is a place to keep it.
then the warm garment could work for the cold part without making you keep it on all day. the space it takes may be less of a problem if you have a place to put it.
why did you not just say the small one was better for being inside?
because your first need was cold weather outside. the new detail gives a way to use the warm garment outside and put it away inside.
only give the choice from what i told you.
the warm garment sounds useful, because you can use it outside and take it off in the warm building.
is that a rule for every day?
no. it is a choice for the weather, place, and details you gave for this day.
three people are waiting. my brother is first, i am next, and my sister is last. who is between the other two?
you are between your brother and your sister.
who comes after me?
your sister comes after you.
now my brother leaves the line. am i still between them?
no. your brother is no longer in the line. you are now first, with your sister after you.
can you say my sister is first too?
not from that change. she is still after you, so you are first while she is next.
now i leave, and she does not.
then your sister is the only person left in the line. she is both first and last.
how can both first and last be true?
when there is only one person, nobody is before or after that person in the line. that makes the same person first and last.
what if my brother comes back at the end?
then your sister is first, and your brother is last. returning at the end does not put him back in his old place.
only give the order now.
your sister is first. your brother is next and last.
write a story about a worker being asked to bring a tool but not knowing what the task is. keep the tool general.

a worker was cleaning a room when another person asked him to bring a tool from the shelf. there were different tools there, and he did not know which one would help. he asked what needed to be done. the other person showed him a small part of a chair that had come apart and explained the kind of tool needed to put it back. now the worker could choose the right object from the shelf. just being asked for a tool had not been enough, but the details about what needed to change made the choice clear.
why did he not bring any tool at all?
different tools can do different things. without knowing the task, he might bring something that could not help.
did asking mean that he did not want to help?
no. he asked because he wanted enough information to choose something useful.
can you know how the tool works from this story?
not in detail. the story keeps the tool general and does not explain its parts or how to use it.
what question could he ask before going to the shelf?
what do you need to do, and what kind of tool would help?
make the last part about him asking before using it.
he brought the tool and asked whether it was the one needed. after hearing yes, he listened to how the other person wanted to use it before helping with the chair.
why is the word tool not enough by itself?
it gives a general group of objects, not the specific object or its use.
my friend draws very well. when i look at my own picture after seeing hers, i want to put it away.
it can be hard to look at your own work right after seeing someone else do something well. what did you like about your picture before you saw hers?
i liked the tree. i had worked on the shape of it for a long time.
that part of your picture has not changed. you can still see the work you put into it, even while you like what your friend made.
i do not want to say my picture is better than hers.
you do not need to. you can like a part of your own picture without saying it is better than what another person made.
use simple words for that.
you can like your tree without saying it is better than her picture.
can you help me write a sentence to myself?
i liked this tree before seeing another picture, and i can still like it now.
what if i want to learn from how she draws?
you can ask about one part you want to understand, such as how she began the shape. learning from her does not mean putting your own work away.
write a question that does not ask her to draw it for me.
could you tell me how you started this part? i would like to try learning it myself.
someone asked the name of a person in my photo, and i do not remember. what should i say?
i do not remember their name right now.
can i say i never knew it?
only if that is true. you may have known the name before but not remember it now. that is different from never knowing it.
i knew it before. i just cannot bring it to mind.
then you can say: i knew their name, but i cannot remember it right now.
what if i remember where we met?
you can give that part while leaving the name open. for example: i met them at school, but i cannot remember their name right now. use the real place where you met.
i met them at the library. write that without the school example.
i met them at the library, but i cannot remember their name right now.
should i choose a name that sounds right so the conversation can move on?
it is better to say you do not remember than to give a name as a fact when you are not sure. you can keep talking about what you do know.
only give the library sentence again.
i met them at the library, but i cannot remember their name right now.
is everyone are ready correct?
use everyone is ready. everyone is about all the people, but it goes with is in that sentence.
what about everything are ready?
use everything is ready too.
why can i say all the people are ready then?
all the people has people as the group you are talking about, so are works there. everyone is a different word and goes with is in this sentence.
show those two correct sentences together.
everyone is ready. all the people are ready.
now make them about yesterday.
everyone was ready yesterday. all the people were ready yesterday.
make a question from everyone is ready.
is everyone ready?
now ask about all the people.
are all the people ready?
can you give only the sentence with everything again?
everything is ready.
write a story about someone going to the shop with a list and not finding one thing. they should still do the parts they can.

a man went to the shop with a list for dinner. he needed rice, vegetables, and milk. the rice and vegetables were there, but he could not find milk. he asked a worker, who told him there was no milk left that afternoon. he bought the things he could get and sent a message home about the milk. his sister said they still had enough for that evening and could buy more the next day. he came home with part of the list and useful information about the rest.
why did he send a message instead of saying everything was done?
because the milk was not bought. saying what he found and what he could not find helped the person at home plan with the real information.
did not finding milk mean he bought nothing?
no. he bought rice and vegetables. one thing he could not find did not take away the parts he did finish.
write his message to his sister.
i bought rice and vegetables, but the shop has no milk left this afternoon. do we have enough for dinner?
why ask whether there is enough at home?
he did not know that detail yet. her answer could help him choose whether he needed another shop or could go home.
finish without adding a visit to another shop.
she told him they had enough milk at home. he put the food away when he returned and left milk on the list for the next day.
what information did he bring home as well as food?
he brought the information that the shop had no milk left that afternoon.
there is a plant on my shelf and the window is open. i close the window. is the plant still on the shelf?
yes, from what you said, the plant is still on the shelf. closing the window does not say that you moved the plant.
can you know the plant is near the window?
no. you gave a shelf and a window, but not how close they are.
now i say the shelf is next to the window.
then the plant on that shelf is near the window, from your new detail.
can you know it is getting enough light?
not from that alone. being near a window does not tell us how much light comes through or what the plant needs.
so what can you say for sure from my words?
the plant is on a shelf near the window, and you closed the window.
what if i move the plant to my desk now?
then its new place is your desk. the window is still closed unless you tell me it was opened again.
why not put the shelf near the desk too?
moving the plant does not move the shelf. those are different objects.
only give the place of the plant now.
the plant is on your desk.
my friend remembered to bring my book. give me a short thank you.
thank you for bringing my book.
can it sound a little more like a message to a close friend?
thanks for bringing my book. i am happy to have it back.
i do not want to say happy. keep it about what they did.
thanks for bringing my book today.
now make it shorter.
thanks for bringing it.
does that say it was late?
no. it thanks them for bringing it without saying anything about whether it was early or late.
what if i want to add that i needed it today?
thanks for bringing my book. i needed it today.
only give the short thank you again.
thanks for bringing it.
what is the opposite of empty? just the word.
full.
now use both in one sentence about two cups.
one cup is empty, and the other is full.
can both be full if i say only one is empty?
if there are just those two cups and one is empty, they are not both full. the empty one is not full.
what if i make the empty cup full too?
then both can be full, if the other one is still full.
why add if?
because you changed one cup but did not say whether anything happened to the other. if it stayed full, both are full now.
keep the other cup full. give the answer without an explanation.
both cups are full.
now just goodbye.
goodbye.
